memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Lord saw this and rejected them because he was angered by his sons and daughters. 'I will hide my face from them,' he said, 'and see what their end will be; for they are a perverse generation, children who are unfaithful. They made me jealous by what is no god and angered me with their worthless idols.'" — Deut 32:19-21a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God responds to His people's unfaithfulness with grief and holy anger. Notice the relational language even here — He is "angered by his sons and daughters." This is not the cold displeasure of a distant ruler, but the wounded response of a Father whose children have betrayed His love. Their idolatry provoked Him, not because His ego was bruised, but because idolatry is a rejection of the only One who is truly God, in favour of "worthless idols" that are "no god" at all.

There is something important here about the nature of God's anger. It is roused by love, not by pettiness. A father who felt nothing when his children destroyed themselves with worthless things would not be loving. God's jealousy is the jealousy of committed love — He wants His people for Himself because He knows that He alone is their true good, and that idols will only ruin them.

The phrase "I will hide my face" describes a painful reality: the withdrawing of God's felt presence and favour as a consequence of persistent sin. This is a solemn thing, meant to awaken His people to what they are losing.

Yet even God's discipline is aimed at restoration. And here is the glory of the gospel: on the cross, Jesus experienced the ultimate hiding of God's face, crying out, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" (Matt 27:46). He endured that abandonment so that we, who deserve it, need never be finally forsaken. Because Christ was rejected in our place, God's face is turned toward us in grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I understand God's anger at sin as flowing from His love?
2. Have I ever treasured "worthless idols" over the God who is my true good?
3. How does Christ enduring God's hidden face on the cross comfort me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Your anger at sin flows from love, and that You desire me for my good. Forgive my idols. Thank You that Christ was forsaken so that I never will be. Turn Your face toward me in grace. Amen.
